partners.mechanism_chain: KCNJ11 (HGNC:6314) —BINDS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP channel) activity (GO:0005400); ABCC8 (HGNC:5540) —BINDS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP channel) activity (GO:0005400); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —BINDS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP channel) activity (GO:0005400); ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP channel) activity (GO:0005400) —DISRUPTS→ Pancreatic beta-cell depolarization and insulin secretion (GO:0007307); Pancreatic beta-cell depolarization and insulin secretion (GO:0007307) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperglycemia (HP:0000823); Pancreatic beta-cell depolarization and insulin secretion (GO:0007307) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0001289); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —DECREASES→ Pancreatic beta-cell depolarization and insulin secretion (GO:0007307); Leucine (CHEBI:17561) —INCREASES→ Pancreatic beta-cell depolarization and insulin secretion (GO:0007307). Mutations in KCNJ11 and ABCC8 lead to loss of function of the KATP channel. In transient neonatal diabetes, this leads to reduced ATP sensitivity, causing the channel to remain open even at high ATP levels. This prevents beta-cell depolarization and impairs insulin secretion, resulting in hyperglycemia. In contrast, in leucine-induced hypoglycemia, the KATP channel is normally inhibited by leucine, leading to depolarization and insulin secretion. However, loss-of-function mutations in KCNJ11/ABCC8 make the channel constitutively open, leading to persistent depolarization and excessive insulin secretion, even in the absence of leucine stimulus, causing hypoglycemia.
